IPv4 address container used by EoE, storing the address in network byte order in a 32-bit field named addr. Accessor macros in this header read/write individual octets and set the value with correct endianness. No ownership or dynamic allocation implied.

Packed Ethernet MAC address structure for EoE. Contains a 6-byte addr array. Packing is controlled by OSAL_PACKED macros to ensure on-wire layout. No dynamic lifetime; typically embedded in other structs.

EoE IP parameter container used to request/set IP configuration via mailbox. Bitfields indicate which parameters are valid. Holds MAC, IPv4 address, subnet, default gateway, DNS IP, and DNS name. Storage-only; no packing required. Passed to ecx_EOEsetIp/ecx_EOEgetIp.

Packed EoE mailbox frame structure for interpreting raw EoE packets. Contains the mailbox header, frame info fields (with a union for either frameinfo2 or result), and payload buffer data sized to EC_MAXEOEDATA. Intended for on-wire parsing/serialization.

functions.name: osal_get_monotonic_time
functions.signature: void osal_get_monotonic_time(ec_timet *ts);
functions.description: Retrieves a strictly monotonic timestamp (not subject to wall-clock changes) and stores it in the provided ec_timet structure. Intended for measuring time intervals.
requirements: ts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable ec_timet storage.
The function writes a timestamp into *ts; caller must provide storage.
Use this time source for interval/duration measurements rather than wall time.

functions.name: osal_current_time
functions.signature: ec_timet osal_current_time(void);
functions.description: Returns the current (wall) time. Used for initializing EtherCAT Distributed Clocks (DC) and for logging.
requirements: Caller uses the returned ec_timet value directly; no arguments are required.
The exact epoch/origin of ec_timet is defined by the OSAL/ec_timet type (details not shown here).

functions.name: osal_time_diff
functions.signature: void osal_time_diff(ec_timet *start, ec_timet *end, ec_timet *diff);
functions.description: Computes the difference between two timestamps and stores the result in diff. Intended for duration calculation (end - start).
requirements: start must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized ec_timet.
end must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized ec_timet.
diff must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable ec_timet storage.
Behavior if end precedes start depends on implementation (unknown; not documented).

functions.name: osal_timer_start
functions.signature: void osal_timer_start(osal_timert *self, uint32 timeout_usec);
functions.description: Initializes or restarts a timer to expire after timeout_usec microseconds from now, by setting an internal stop_time in the osal_timert.
requirements: self must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an osal_timert instance.
timeout_usec is an unsigned 32-bit microsecond timeout; allowable range beyond the type limit is not documented.
Call this before checking expiration with osal_timer_is_expired (inferred).

functions.name: osal_timer_is_expired
functions.signature: boolean osal_timer_is_expired(osal_timert *self);
functions.description: Checks whether the previously started timer has reached or passed its stop time.
requirements: self must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an osal_timert initialized via osal_timer_start (inferred).
Returns TRUE if expired, FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: osal_usleep
functions.signature: int osal_usleep(uint32 usec);
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread for approximately usec microseconds.
requirements: usec is an unsigned 32-bit duration in microseconds; valid range beyond the type limit is not documented.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller should check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: osal_monotonic_sleep
functions.signature: int osal_monotonic_sleep(ec_timet *ts);
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread until the specified absolute monotonic time ts is reached.
requirements: ts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an ec_timet representing an absolute monotonic deadline (inferred).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller should check the return value and handle errors.
If ts is in the past, behavior is implementation-defined (unknown; not documented).

functions.description: Allocates size bytes of memory and returns a pointer to the allocated block, or NULL on failure.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; behavior for size == 0 is not documented (unknown).

requirements: ptr should be a pointer previously returned by osal_malloc or a compatible allocator used by this OSAL (inferred).
Passing NULL is not documented; behavior is unknown.
Do not double-free the same pointer (inferred).

functions.name: osal_thread_create
functions.signature: int osal_thread_create(void *thandle, int stacksize, void *func, void *param);
functions.description: Creates a new thread that starts execution at func with param, using a requested stack size. On success, stores a thread identifier/handle via thandle.
requirements: thandle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to storage suitable for a thread handle/ID (exact type/size unknown; provided as void*).
stacksize is the requested stack size in bytes (presumably); valid range and minimums are not documented (unknown).
func must be a valid, non-NULL thread entry point compatible with the platform’s expectations (exact function type is not specified; unknown).
param is passed to the thread entry function and may be NULL.
Returns 1 on success and 0 on failure; caller must check the return value.

functions.description: Locks the specified mutex, blocking if necessary until it becomes available.

functions.description: Unlocks the specified mutex that was previously locked by the calling thread.
requirements: mutex must be a valid, non-NULL mutex handle obtained from osal_mutex_create (inferred).

functions.name: ec_setupheader
functions.signature: void ec_setupheader(void *p);
functions.description: Initializes the Ethernet/EtherCAT header in the provided buffer. Typically used to prepare a transmit buffer with the correct protocol header before populating payload and sending. Details of the exact header fields are not shown in this header; they are set based on the library’s defaults.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer large enough to contain the Ethernet/EtherCAT header (exact size unknown from this header).
The buffer pointed to by p must be suitably aligned for header writes.
Call this before sending a frame that requires a correctly initialized header.

functions.name: ecx_setupnic
functions.signature: int ecx_setupnic(ecx_portt *port, const char *ifname, int secondary);
functions.description: Opens and configures the network interface for EtherCAT communication, initializes buffers, state, and synchronization primitives in the provided port structure. Use this once per port before any send/receive operations. Returns an int status (success/non-success; exact codes not specified here).
requirements: port must be a valid, writable pointer to an ecx_portt structure.
ifname must reference a valid network interface name present on the system (e.g., "eth0").
secondary indicates whether to configure a secondary (redundant) interface; expected values are 0 (primary) or non-zero (secondary), exact semantics beyond that are not specified here.
Must be called before any of: ecx_getindex, ecx_outframe, ecx_outframe_red, ecx_waitinframe, ecx_srconfirm, or ecx_closenic.
Caller should check the return value and abort further NIC operations on failure.
Threading: this function initializes mutexes inside port; do not concurrently call it on the same port from multiple threads.

functions.name: ecx_closenic
functions.signature: int ecx_closenic(ecx_portt *port);
functions.description: Closes the network interface associated with the given port and releases related resources (sockets, buffers, synchronization primitives). Returns an int status (specific codes not shown). Call when EtherCAT communications on this port are finished.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an ecx_portt previously initialized by ecx_setupnic.
Do not use the port for send/receive operations after a successful close.
Caller should ensure no other threads are actively using the port when closing.
Caller should check the return value to confirm close success.

functions.name: ecx_setbufstat
functions.signature: void ecx_setbufstat(ecx_portt *port, uint8 idx, int bufstat);
functions.description: Sets the status field of the receive/transmit buffer slot identified by idx within the given port. Useful for managing buffer lifecycle or signaling buffer availability. The exact meaning of bufstat values is not defined in this header.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt.
idx must refer to a valid buffer index: 0 <= idx < EC_MAXBUF.
bufstat must be a valid status code as expected by the library (specific values not defined here).
Only call after ecx_setupnic has successfully initialized the port.

functions.name: ecx_getindex
functions.signature: uint8 ecx_getindex(ecx_portt *port);
functions.description: Obtains a free/transmit buffer index for use in subsequent send/receive operations. Intended usage is to acquire an index, fill the corresponding transmit buffer, send a frame, then wait for and process a response, and finally release/update the buffer status.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt.
Caller should use the returned index with other functions that take idx (e.g., ecx_outframe, ecx_waitinframe, ecx_srconfirm).
The returned index is valid only within the context of the specified port and until the buffer lifecycle is completed per library conventions (exact release mechanism not documented here).
Not thread-safe to reuse the same idx concurrently; each concurrent operation should acquire its own idx.

functions.name: ecx_outframe
functions.signature: int ecx_outframe(ecx_portt *port, uint8 idx, int sock);
functions.description: Transmits the frame stored in the port’s transmit buffer at index idx over the specified socket. Returns an int status (success/failure; exact semantics not defined here). Typical usage: get idx via ecx_getindex, populate the tx buffer for idx, then call ecx_outframe to send.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt.
idx must be a valid buffer index: 0 <= idx < EC_MAXBUF and should have been acquired via ecx_getindex.
The transmit buffer for idx must be fully prepared (including header via ec_setupheader and payload) before calling.
sock must be a valid socket handle compatible with the port’s network configuration (the meaning of special values, if any, is not defined here).
Caller should check the return value and handle send failures appropriately.

functions.name: ecx_outframe_red
functions.signature: int ecx_outframe_red(ecx_portt *port, uint8 idx);
functions.description: Transmits the frame at buffer index idx using the redundancy mechanism (e.g., sending via primary and secondary paths). Returns an int status (not further specified). Use when redundancy is configured on the port.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt with redundancy configured (port->redport set by setup).
idx must be a valid buffer index: 0 <= idx < EC_MAXBUF and should have been acquired via ecx_getindex.
The transmit buffer for idx must be fully prepared before calling.
Caller should check the return value and handle send failures appropriately.

functions.name: ecx_waitinframe
functions.signature: int ecx_waitinframe(ecx_portt *port, uint8 idx, int timeout);
functions.description: Blocks until a frame matching the buffer index idx is received or the timeout elapses. Returns an int status indicating receive result (exact return codes and their meanings are not specified in this header). Typical usage: after ecx_outframe or ecx_outframe_red, call ecx_waitinframe to await the response.
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt.
idx must be a valid buffer index that corresponds to an outstanding transmission or expected frame.
timeout must be a non-negative duration; units are not specified in this header (commonly milliseconds or microseconds in similar libraries; unknown here).
Caller must handle timeout and error return values appropriately based on the library’s defined conventions (not provided in this header).

functions.name: ecx_srconfirm
functions.signature: int ecx_srconfirm(ecx_portt *port, uint8 idx, int timeout);
functions.description: Waits for and confirms reception of the expected response corresponding to a previously sent frame at buffer index idx, within the given timeout. This is commonly used as a combined send/receive confirmation step in the EtherCAT exchange sequence. Returns an int status (exact codes not specified).
requirements: port must be a valid pointer to an initialized ecx_portt.
idx must be a valid buffer index associated with a recently sent frame whose response is expected.
timeout must be a non-negative duration; units are not specified in this header.
Caller should interpret the return value per the library’s conventions to detect success, timeout, or error.

functions.name: ecx_setupdatagram
functions.signature: int ecx_setupdatagram(ecx_portt *port, void *frame, uint8 com, uint8 idx, uint16 ADP, uint16 ADO, uint16 length, void *data);
functions.description: Builds a single EtherCAT datagram in the provided frame buffer. The caller specifies the EtherCAT command (com), datagram index (idx), station address (ADP/ADO), payload length, and an optional data buffer. Intended for low-level packet composition prior to transmission on the given port.
requirements: port must be a valid, initialized EtherCAT port context (non-null)
frame must point to a writable frame buffer large enough to hold the datagram and its header
com must be a valid EtherCAT command code (8-bit)
idx must fit in 0..255 (8-bit datagram index)
length must be the number of payload bytes to place in the datagram
if length > 0 then data must be non-null and point to at least length bytes of readable data (for write-type commands) or writable space (for read-type commands)
ADP and ADO are 16-bit address fields and must contain the target address/offset appropriate for the chosen command
Function usage details like return value conventions are not documented here and are unknown

functions.name: ecx_adddatagram
functions.signature: uint16 ecx_adddatagram(ecx_portt *port, void *frame, uint8 com, uint8 idx, boolean more, uint16 ADP, uint16 ADO, uint16 length, void *data);
functions.description: Appends an EtherCAT datagram to an existing frame buffer, optionally indicating that more datagrams will follow. Used to create a combined frame with multiple datagrams for a single transmission on the given port.
requirements: port must be a valid, initialized EtherCAT port context (non-null)
frame must point to an existing EtherCAT frame buffer with sufficient remaining space for the new datagram
com must be a valid EtherCAT command code (8-bit)
idx must fit in 0..255 (8-bit datagram index)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for a generic binary blob used across many EtherCAT-related stubs.
# Goals:
# - Produce buffers that are likely valid and interesting for these APIs:
#   * Ethernet/EtherCAT header prep (>=64 bytes)
#   * Datagram frame/payload composition (header+payload room)
#   * Mailbox/EoE/SDO/PDO read/write buffers with plausible sizes
# - Include multiple sized segments with realistic lengths (e.g., 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1500 bytes)
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes
# - Deterministic under seed, but random each call with different seed
# - No file I/O; return bytes only
# - Favor non-empty outputs and include NULs where needed (C-strings)

ETHERTYPE_ETHERCAT = 0x88A4


def _rand_mac(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Unicast, locally administered MAC (x2 bit set, x1 bit clear)
    first = rnd.randrange(0, 256) & 0xFE | 0x02
    return bytes([first]) + rnd.randbytes(5)


def _ethernet_header(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a plausible Ethernet header for EtherCAT frames
    dst = _rand_mac(rnd)
    src = _rand_mac(rnd)
    etype = ETHERTYPE_ETHERCAT
    return dst + src + struct.pack("!H", etype)


def _ecat_comhdr(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimalistic EtherCAT datagram header-like bytes (not strict, but plausible)
    # elength(2), command(1), index(1), ADP(2), ADO(2), dlength(2), irpt(2)
    elength = rnd.randrange(1, 512)
    command = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
    index = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
    ADP = rnd.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    ADO = rnd.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    dlength = rnd.randrange(0, 512)
    irpt = 0
    return (
        struct.pack("!H", elength)
        + struct.pack("!B", command)
        + struct.pack("!B", index)
        + struct.pack("!H", ADP)
        + struct.pack("!H", ADO)
        + struct.pack("!H", dlength)
        + struct.pack("!H", irpt)
    )


def _c_string(rnd: random.Random, maxlen: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a C-string-like segment terminated with NUL
    length = rnd.randrange(1, maxlen)
    # Mix alnum and safe symbols
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-/"
    s = bytes(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s + b"\x00"


def _pad(b: bytes, size: int) -> bytes:
    if len(b) >= size:
        return b[:size]
    return b + b"\x00" * (size - len(b))


def _build_header_friendly_blob(rnd: random.Random, min_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a buffer starting with an Ethernet header and an EC-like header,
    # then pad to at least min_size. This helps ec_setupheader and frame buffers.
    eth = _ethernet_header(rnd)
    ech = _ecat_comhdr(rnd)
    blob = eth + ech
    # Add some payload bytes to allow space for subsequent payload fields
    payload_len = max(0, min_size - len(blob))
    if payload_len < 32:
        payload_len = 32
    blob += rnd.randbytes(payload_len)
    return _pad(blob, max(min_size, len(blob)))


def _build_payload_variants(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Create a set of payloads of varying sizes for read/write operations
    sizes = []
    # Typical sizes used by stubs: up to 64, 1024, 1500, and small edge cases
    sizes.extend([1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024, 1400, 1500])
    # Random additional sizes
    for _ in range(6):
        sizes.append(rnd.randrange(1, 1536))
    # Deduplicate and clamp to <=1500
    sizes = sorted(set(min(s, 1500) for s in sizes))
    payloads = []
    for s in sizes:
        # For read buffers, content can be arbitrary; include a few with recognizable patterns
        mode = rnd.randrange(0, 4)
        if mode == 0:
            buf = rnd.randbytes(s)
        elif mode == 1:
            # Repeated pattern
            pattern = struct.pack("!I", rnd.getrandbits(32))
            buf = (pattern * ((s + len(pattern) - 1) // len(pattern)))[:s]
        elif mode == 2:
            # Zero-filled
            buf = b"\x00" * s
        else:
            # Incrementing bytes
            start = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
            buf = bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(s))
        payloads.append(buf)
    return payloads


def _build_mailbox_like(rnd: random.Random, capacity: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a mailbox-like buffer: [mbx length(2)][address(2)][prio(1)][type(1)] + data
    length = rnd.randrange(1, min(1024, capacity - 6)) if capacity > 6 else 0
    mbx = (
        struct.pack("!H", length)
        + struct.pack("!H", rnd.randrange(0, 0x10000))
        + struct.pack("!B", rnd.randrange(0, 256))
        + struct.pack("!B", rnd.randrange(0, 256))
    )
    data = rnd.randbytes(max(0, capacity - len(mbx)))
    return _pad(mbx + data, capacity)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy: Build a composite buffer consisting of multiple sections that the fuzzer can slice:
    # - Section A: header-friendly frame (>=64 bytes)
    # - Section B: a few filename C-strings for FoE (NUL-terminated)
    # - Section C: a mailbox-like buffer (~EC_MAXMBX scale, but bounded)
    # - Section D: several payload variants concatenated
    # Keep total size <= 4096

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Section A: Frame header space; choose between 64, 128, or 256 minimum
    min_header = rnd.choice([64, 128, 256])
    parts.append(_build_header_friendly_blob(rnd, min_header))

    # Section B: Filenames for FoE; include 2-3 plausible names
    file_count = rnd.randrange(2, 4)
    for _ in range(file_count):
        maxlen = rnd.choice([16, 32, 64, 128])
        parts.append(_c_string(rnd, maxlen))

    # Section C: Mailbox-sized buffer (bounded to 1024 for perf)
    parts.append(_build_mailbox_like(rnd, rnd.choice([128, 256, 512, 1024])))

    # Section D: Payload variants
    payloads = _build_payload_variants(rnd)

    # To avoid exceeding 4096, add payloads until close to the limit
    total = sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    for p in payloads:
        if total + len(p) > 4096:
            break
        parts.append(p)
        total += len(p)

    # Final assembly. Shuffle some of the smaller parts to vary distribution while
    # keeping the initial header-friendly block first to satisfy ec_setupheader usage.
    head = parts[0]
    tail = parts[1:]
    rnd.shuffle(tail)
    out = head + b"".join(tail)

    # Ensure final size cap
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    # Guarantee non-empty output and at least 64 bytes for header users
    if len(out) < 64:
        out += b"\x00" * (64 - len(out))

    return out

def _nic_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:

    # Common patterns

    return name[:64]


def _filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a plausible filename path
    d = rng.choice(DIRS)
    base = rng.choice(FILE_BASENAMES)
    # sometimes add numeric suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base += f"_{_rand_int(rng, 0, 9999)}"
    ext = rng.choice(FILE_EXTS)
    name = f"{d}{base}.{ext}"
    # sometimes nested subdir
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        sub = rng.choice(["backup", "old", "new", "test", "v1", "v2", "stable", "beta"])  # simple tokens
        name = name.replace(d, d + sub + "/", 1) if d else sub + "/" + name
    # Ensure no NULs and reasonable length
    return name[:256]


def _payload_lines(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # First line: high-likelihood valid NIC
    lines.append(_nic_name(rng))
    # Additional NIC variants to let FUZZ_PARAM_STR draw from a pool if it splits
    for _ in range(_rand_int(rng, 1, 4)):
        lines.append(_nic_name(rng))
    # A few filenames for FoE operations
    for _ in range(_rand_int(rng, 2, 6)):
        lines.append(_filename(rng))
    # Some bare names (no path) with different extensions
    for _ in range(_rand_int(rng, 1, 3)):
        b = rng.choice(FILE_BASENAMES)
        ext = rng.choice(FILE_EXTS)
        lines.append(f"{b}.{ext}")
    # Include special names that might be accepted by devices
    lines.extend([
        "firmware.bin",
        "config.dat",
        "index.htm",
        "index.html",
        "eeprom.sii",
        "pdo_map.xml",
    ])
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in lines:
        if s not in seen:
            uniq.append(s)
            seen.add(s)
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    lines = _payload_lines(rng)
    # Join lines with newlines so consumers can slice tokens; ensure trailing newline for robustness
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    # Ensure size limit
    data = text.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return data
